title: The Bay of Fundy Moves More Water Than Every River on Earth

scenes.text: One bay moves more water than every river combined.
It's the Bay of Fundy, in eastern Canada.
Twice a day, over 100 billion tons of seawater flow in and out.
That's more than all the world's freshwater rivers put together.
The tide can rise as much as 53 feet, about a five-story building.
A beach you can walk across at low tide is deep underwater six hours later.

description:
One bay moves more water than every river combined.
Twice a day, more than 100 billion tons of seawater flow in and out of the Bay of Fundy, and the tide can rise up to 53 feet.
Have you ever seen a tide this big?
first_comment: A tide that rises 53 feet. Would you walk out on the seafloor at low tide?
